title: Research: odd-kernel coefficient-bit tariff exceeds dyadic on j=0..32 (answers #2687 OQ2; no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Bounded follow-up under priority revision 6 answering [#2687](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2687) OQ2: under a concrete physical tariff, do larger-`q` coefficient-table bit-sizes ever pay for themselves despite identical typed child/XOR counts?

This package attaches one named ADDRESS affine coefficient-bit tariff (`ADDRESS_affine_coeff_num_den_bit_sum`: for each diagonal/control coeff `c=p/q` in lowest terms charge `bit_length(|p|)+bit_length(q)`) to the PR840/`#2687` `address_word` lowering. Program bills:

```text
T_fused(q,j)    = 2·T_word(q·2^j) + T_word(q·2^{j+1})
T_baseline(q,j) = 4·T_word(q·2^j)
```

On certified kernels `{1,3,5,7,9,15}` and every `j∈{0,…,32}`, every odd kernel strictly exceeds the dyadic fused and baseline bills (**165+165** comparisons; min fused margin **14** at `(q=3,j=0)`). Typed fused child/XOR counts stay identical (`3/18/2`). `T_word` is not monotone in `|k|` (`T(4)=32 < T(2)=38 < T(1)=45`), so the claim is the program comparison under this tariff, not a bare word-size argument.

**Scope.** This is a coefficient-table size proxy grounded in PR840’s num/den-bit remark, not a fully charged BIT-supplier / routing bill. “Never pay for themselves” means: on this named tariff, these kernels, and `j=0..32`. [#2687](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2687) OQ1 (admitted supplier hosting bill) stays open.

**No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/odd-kernel-coeff-bit-tariff/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/odd-kernel-coeff-bit-tariff/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/odd-kernel-coeff-bit-tariff/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/odd-kernel-coeff-bit-tariff/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/odd-kernel-coeff-bit-tariff
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_ODD_KERNEL_COEFF_BIT_TARIFF kernels=[1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 15] j=0..32 odd_fused_exceeds_dyadic=165 odd_baseline_exceeds_dyadic=165 no_new_kappa
PASS_ODD_KERNEL_COEFF_BIT_TARIFF_INDEPENDENT kernels=[1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 15] j=0..32 odd_fused_exceeds_dyadic=165 no_new_kappa
PASS_ODD_KERNEL_COEFF_BIT_TARIFF_PACKAGE_TESTS groups=4
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/odd-kernel-coeff-bit-tariff outcome=completed
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`.

## Open next questions

1. Does any alternate physical tariff (max-height / packing / modulus-dependent) make a certified odd kernel beat dyadic at some `j`?
2. Can an admitted BIT supplier host a small odd-kernel shear with a favorable fully charged bill versus dyadic? (still #2687 OQ1)
